sn35.118:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha on Mount Vulture Peak.
sn35.118:1.2: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, stood to one side, and said to him:
sn35.118:1.3: “Venerable sir, what is the cause and reason why some beings here do not attain Nibbāna in this very life?
sn35.118:1.4: And what is the cause and reason why some beings here attain Nibbāna in this very life?”
sn35.118:2.1: “There are, lord of the devas, forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.118:2.2: If a bhikkhu seeks delight in them, welcomes them, and remains holding to them,
sn35.118:2.3: his consciousness becomes dependent upon them and clings to them.
sn35.118:2.4: A bhikkhu with clinging does not attain Nibbāna.
sn35.118:3.1: “There are, lord of the devas, sounds cognizable by the ear …
sn35.118:3.2: mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.118:3.3: If a bhikkhu seeks delight in them, welcomes them, and remains holding to them,
sn35.118:3.4: his consciousness becomes dependent upon them and clings to them.
sn35.118:3.5: A bhikkhu with clinging does not attain Nibbāna.
sn35.118:3.6: “This is the cause and reason, lord of the devas, why some beings here do not attain Nibbāna in this very life.
sn35.118:4.1: “There are, lord of the devas, forms cognizable by the eye …
sn35.118:5.2: mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.118:5.3: If a bhikkhu does not seek delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain holding to them,
sn35.118:5.4: his consciousness does not become dependent upon them or cling to them.
sn35.118:5.5: A bhikkhu without clinging attains Nibbāna.
sn35.118:5.6: “This is the cause and reason, lord of the devas, why some beings here attain Nibbāna in this very life.”
